title: Compiler warnings, language standards and portability flags
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its constraints.
Trace the example and reason about its data flow.
Identify complexity, boundary or safety considerations.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: C compilers support language standard modes and diagnostic options. Flags such as -std=c17, -Wall, -Wextra and -Wpedantic request a selected language version and additional diagnostics on many GCC- and Clang-like toolchains.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit build settings make behaviour more reproducible and reveal suspicious code before runtime. Compiler flags differ by toolchain and should be documented rather than assumed universal.
understand.analogy: Treat an algorithm or data structure as a set of operations that must preserve a clearly stated contract.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace formal complexity analysis, C object rules or algorithm preconditions.

explain.narrative:
C compilers support language standard modes and diagnostic options. Flags such as -std=c17, -Wall, -Wextra and -Wpedantic request a selected language version and additional diagnostics on many GCC- and Clang-like toolchains.

Before implementation, state input constraints, empty-case behaviour, ownership and invariants. Compile with warnings and test representative, boundary and failure cases.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The command selects C17 and enables several warning groups. The exact available flags and diagnostics depend on the compiler version.

practise.guidedTask: Explain the purpose of the language standard flag and warning flags.
practise.independentTask: Build the same small program with and without warnings. Record the differences and resolve each meaningful warning.
hints: A warning is diagnostic evidence, not proof that the program is wrong or correct.
Use the same documented compiler options in local and automated builds.
Avoid compiler-specific extensions when portability is a requirement.
